title: Fit the air shroud in a rack server: tuck both tabs under the fan cage, then lower it to seat
instruction: Refit the air shroud: tilt it, put both front tabs into the slots under the fan cage top, then lower it until it is seated.
context: The air shroud ducts a server's fan air over its processors and memory, and it comes out for almost every job inside: Dell's PowerEdge R760 manual lists "Remove the air shroud" before memory, processor, heat-sink, riser and expansion-card work, and warns: "Never operate your system with the air shroud removed. The system may get overheated quickly". Refitting it is the manual's install step: "Tilt the air shroud at an angle and align the air shroud tabs with the system slots. Ensure that the air shroud tabs are below the surface of the cooling cage fan assembly. Lower the air shroud into the system until it is firmly seated." Lowered flat, both tabs land on top of the fan cage and the shroud sits proud. The robot carries the 426 mm duct with both hands, gets both tabs in at once and lowers it between the heat sinks and memory rows without racking it, as technicians do in the data centres that run AI workloads.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. A Dell PowerEdge R760 2U rack server (steel chassis 434 wide without its rack ears, 722.7 from its front panel to its rear wall, 86.8 high; unpowered and unplugged, system cover off) lies flat on the bench between the arms, front panel toward the robot at x -150, centred on y 0. Inside, from the front: the drive cage under its closed steel top (to x -15); the backplane's cable space; the cooling fan cage of six fans (x 69.5 to 144.5; its steel top 82 above the chassis floor, with two slots 22 wide and 6.5 high in its back face just under that top, centred at y +107 and -107); the shroud's bay over the system board: two finned aluminium processor heat sinks (61 wide, 100 long, 71 high, centred at x 228, y +-107) and four rows of eight DDR5 RDIMMs (133 long, 46 high; outer rows y +-148.5 to +-207, inner rows y +-7.5 to +-65.5); then the riser cages from x 345.5 to the rear wall. The server's own standard (non-GPU) air shroud, black moulded plastic, 426 wide, 165 front to back, 79 high, 0.30 kg, rests right way up on the drive cage's closed top, its middle at x -45, y 0, its tabbed front edge toward the robot: a top panel over the heat sinks and inner memory rows, a duct wall each side of each heat sink, an open trough (wing) over each outer memory row whose back wall is 2.5 thick, an end wall at each end, and two front tabs (16 wide, 7 long, 2 thick) on its front edge at y +107 and -107. Seated, its end walls stand on the chassis floor 3 inside the side walls, its front edge 1 behind the fan cage's back face, each tab 6 through its slot. Every collider is listed in README.md.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from photos and a 2 mm feeler gauge. A tab is in when its tip is at least 3 mm past the fan cage's back face, inside its slot, under the cage's top. Seated: all four bottom corners of the shroud's end walls within 2 mm of the chassis floor (the 2 mm gauge does not pass under any). Still: no point of the shroud moves more than 1 mm in 0.5 s. 1.0 (success): both tabs in, seated, both grippers at least 3 cm clear of the shroud, and still, all held for 1 s. 0.5: both tabs in and seated, but not yet let go and still for 1 s. 0.25: both tabs in, let go and still for 1 s, but not seated (its back resting high). 0: anything else, including only one tab in, the tabs on top of the fan cage (lowered flat), or the shroud dropped (falling faster than 0.6 m/s) or knocked off the chassis at any time.
reset_notes: Lift the shroud out by its edges and set it back right way up on the drive cage's closed top, its middle at x -45, y 0, tabs toward the robot. Nothing is consumed or fastened.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The chassis and all its parts are one fixed body of boxes at true size; the shroud is one rigid body of plates (no flex). Its height, walls, tabs, slots and 0.30 kg, and the heat sinks' and modules' sizes, are estimates from Dell's drawings, to be measured on a real R760. In the simulation it may also be lowered level 12 mm back and slid forward; the real shroud may not allow that. The demo reads the shroud's pose to correct its hands.
